Take the legal way round. Never against traffic. More Driving against traffic is an offence under the Motor Vehicles Act, and dangerous driving carries a fine or jail. No U-turn where a sign or signal forbids it. Dip your headlights in good time for oncoming traffic and when close behind someone; keep high beam off on lit roads. What glare does

Call 112, and pull aside for a siren. More 112 reaches police, fire and ambulance across Telangana; 108 still reaches an ambulance. Blocking an ambulance or fire engine can mean a ₹10,000 fine or six months. Plan the long crossings before you need to hurry: a rush is when the shortcut against traffic looks tempting, and it puts everyone coming the other way at risk. Short termSigns to the next U-turn, lit bays, enforcement. Long termA nearer opening, a signal or an underpass. See the fixes Sources and limits Short term, weeks and low cost: a sign before each closed median saying how far the next U-turn is; lit, marked U-turn bays; enforcement where people ride against traffic, so the legal way round is the normal one. Long term, years and infrastructure: a U-turn opening nearer, a signal-free U-turn with a bay, a signal-controlled crossing or a U-turn underpass, each drawn on a real road

Why the numbers run highThe open map under-records small connections — median openings and service roads drivers use daily are often missing. That inflates every absolute figure here by an unknown amount. It affects all areas alike, so comparing one to another holds, while individual values do not yet. Where a typical route runs past ten kilometres to cross twenty metres, a hole in the map is the likelier explanation than a real detour, and the row says so. Those are the first places we go back and correct the map. Areas with fewer than thirty measured points are left out: a median over a handful of points is noise.

Take a point on a road modelled as two separate carriageways. Find the nearest point on the opposite carriageway, checked to be genuinely across the road rather than a flyover overhead or an unrelated street. Ask the road network for the shortest legal driving route between the two. Divide driving distance by straight-line distance.
Travel time, walking, and anyone's motives. Why
Distance and geometry only. Congestion and roadworks are deliberately excluded — a median still stands when the construction ends, and that is the claim worth making.

The open map holds 407 pedestrian crossings and 212 footbridges for a metropolitan area of roughly ten million, and none within 400 m of Abids or Secunderabad station. Absence in the map is not absence on the ground, so every claim here is about driving.
We publish what an authority recorded and what we measured. Never what we think that means about anyone's motives. Known limitations, kept in public

pages.title: civic sense: what independent studies actually show

s.t: arcroad · evidence base · grades A and B only

s.h: Civic sense: what the evidence shows, and what it doesn't.
s.t: "No civic sense" is said often and measured rarely. What the studies show: much of what looks like bad behaviour is a response to bad design. Only peer-reviewed studies (A) and official statistics (B).

Where a median gap is closed and the legal U-turn is 1–2 km away, some people ride the wrong way instead. arcroad measures the length of that legal detour, so the design that invites the violation is on the record beside the violation. It does not count wrong-way riding at any place, and it never attributes a crash to a single road feature. The studies Finding Grade Source In 2023 wrong-side driving and lane indiscipline were linked to about 5.5% of police-recorded road deaths, the third-largest cause. Over-speeding was about 68%. B MoRTH, Road Accidents in India 2023 On national highways in 2022, wrong-side driving was the second-largest cause of deaths (about 5.8%). The authors call for enforcement and design changes, not only new laws. A IIT Delhi TRIPP (Jain et al.), World Congress on Injury Prevention Wrong-way driving is common enough in India that countermeasures have to be design

These are police-recorded totals for whole cities and police areas. arcroad shows them for scale only: it does not link any crash, death or violation to a place it measures. The official numbers Finding Grade Source Hyderabad recorded 2,943 road crashes in 2023, with 335 people killed and 2,596 injured, up from 2,516 crashes and 323 deaths in 2022. B MoRTH, Road Accidents in India 2023, million-plus cities table (public-domain extract on OpenCity, checked 3 Nov 2026) Of Hyderabad's 335 deaths in 2023, the police recorded 288 under over-speeding and 8 under wrong-side driving. Across all 50 million-plus cities, wrong-side driving accounted for 1,069 of 17,255 deaths, about 6.2%. B MoRTH 2023, million-plus cities by traffic violation (OpenCity extract, checked 3 Nov 2026) Cyberabad, the police area that covers HITEC City, Kukatpally and Miyapur, recorded fewer fatal crashes in 2025 than in

s.h: Headlight glare on the oncoming driver
s.t: Glare is paid for by the person facing the light, not the one who switched it on. Roads without median screens or street lights push drivers to high beam, so arcroad records lighting beside glare and never claims glare caused a particular number of crashes. The studies Finding Grade Source The law requires headlamps that dip so they do not dazzle the driver of an approaching vehicle. Fines fall under the Motor Vehicles Act. B CMVR 1989 rule 106; MVA 1988 s.177 No separate national data on glare crashes is kept. About half of 2022's road crashes happened between 6 pm and 6 am. B MoRTH reply in Parliament Glare that blinds is different from glare that only annoys. After a bright oncoming lamp the eye needs time to recover, longer for older drivers and for objects at the edge of view, such as a pedestrian. A Skinner & Bullough, SAE 2009-01-0546; NHTSA DOT HS 811 043 A US pilot found about t

Long waits, missing crossings and badly placed bridges produce the violation. That is arcroad's whole point: measure what the design costs people, and the "civic sense" argument changes. The studies Finding Grade Source About 45% of pedestrians who arrive on red cross against it, mostly in the second half of the red phase. A Kumar & Ghosh, Safety Science 2021 Across 55 Kolkata junctions, those with more red-light crossing also had more fatal pedestrian crashes. A Safety Science 124:104610 (2020) Longer red phases go with more violations. Of 2,360 pedestrians observed, about 29% were distracted, and those texting violated more. A Raoniar & Maurya (IIT Guwahati), 2022 and 2024 Where a foot overbridge stands beside a street-level crossing, only about a quarter of pedestrians used the bridge. The choice followed the time it cost, not attitude. A Mumbai video survey of 1,134 pedestrians (Patr

Behaviour responds to enforcement people can see, and to design. It is not fixed by "culture". The studies Finding Grade Source In 2023, 16,025 people killed were not wearing seatbelts. Two-wheeler riders were about 45% of road deaths and pedestrians about 20%. B MoRTH 2023 How arcroad uses this evidence A study's rate is compared with arcroad's own only when the place type and the definition match. Nothing is said about any group of people, community, faith, region or gender. Where studies break results down that way, the breakdown is not carried. Official figures are police-recorded and undercount; the site says "police-recorded". Behaviour arcroad measures is aggregate, by stretch and time, never by person or vehicle. No plates or faces. Every figure is re-checked against the primary report before a release.

pages.title: how it is built: the technology, in plain words

s.t: arcroad runs on open maps, open code and a small amount of cloud computing. No cameras, no sensors, no paid data and nothing to install. Here is every piece, explained for someone who has never written code. The map

A free map of the world that anyone can edit, a bit like Wikipedia for roads. Every road, median and U-turn opening in Hyderabad that arcroad studies comes from it. Read with an open tool called osmium, which turns the raw map file into roads the code can work with. Working out the way round

Code that walks the road network the way a law-abiding driver must: only legal turns, only the allowed direction. It finds how far you really drive to reach the point straight across. Written in Python, a popular programming language, with the number libraries pandas, NumPy and SciPy. Think of a very large spreadsheet that recalculates the same way every time. Checking our own answer

Two independent, free route engines used by map apps around the world. We ask both for the same trips; if they agree with us within 10%, the trip is confirmed. Like asking two other people with maps. 18 of the 20 Hi-Tech City loop trips agree. The 2 that do not are shown, not hidden. Buses

A standard file format that bus operators use to publish routes and stops. It lets arcroad work out how far a bus, and everyone on it, is sent round. Used by the bus part of the loop check, for TGSRTC routes. Proving it on the road

The model's answers were driven and recorded with a phone's GPS. Photos show what the driver saw. Faces and number plates are blurred before anything is published, and raw GPS never is. Results on the driven results page; routes, start points and times are never published. Pre-flight checks

Over 300 small automatic checks run before every update, like a pilot's checklist. If one fails, nothing goes live. Run on every change, on the computer and again in the cloud. A record of every change

Git keeps a history of every edit, so any version can be brought back. Each saved version gets a short code called a commit, like a receipt number. A public open copy lives on GitHub. The poster's code version, b04e705, is one such receipt: anyone can rerun it and get the same numbers. The website
Copies of the site are kept in data centres around the world, so the page loads from somewhere near you, quickly and safely. Every page you are reading. No cookies, no tracking. Small server tasks

A function is a tiny program that runs only when needed, for example when someone signs up as a volunteer. KV storage is a simple locker system: each entry has a numbered key and a small value. Volunteer sign-ups keep only an area, the choices made and a random code. No names, emails or phone numbers. Heavy work on a timer

A container is a sealed lunchbox: the program plus everything it needs, so it runs the same anywhere. A batch job is work that starts by itself on a schedule, like a washing machine on a timer. arcroad's research runner is a container that wakes up on a schedule, runs the long calculations and switches itself off. Where results are kept

Storage for files in the cloud, like a shared drive. The scheduled runner drops its finished results there, ready to be checked before anything is published. Nothing goes from there to this site on its own: results are checked first. Maps on your screen

A free, open tool that draws interactive maps in the browser, so you can zoom and pan without any paid map service. Used on the globe and the map views. No Google Maps data is used anywhere. Telling the original from a copy

Each original file gets a fingerprint: a short code computed from its contents, which changes if even one comma changes. Public timestamp authorities then stamp when that fingerprint existed, like a notary's seal. So anyone can check that the published files are the originals and when they were made.

No Google Maps data, and no paid map or traffic data. No cookies, no analytics, no visitor tracking. No hardware on the road, and nothing a city has to buy or install. All of arcroad's code is open under the MIT licence and the data under the Open Database Licence. See what you may reuse, privacy and what it has cost so far.

pages.title: Measure the loop before it opens · Cyberabad Moves 2026

s.t: Cyberabad Moves 2026 · Innovation Challenge entry

s.h: Measure the loop before it opens.
s.t: Cyberabad Police have proposed turning the roads between Biodiversity Junction, IKEA, Mindspace, Knowledge City and Dallas Center into a one-way loop, and plan to judge it by vehicle speed and traffic density. One thing is not on that list: how much further each journey becomes. arcroad brings a ready, tested and open way to measure it, before the trial, during it and after. In one minute · shortlisted, Citizens Innovation Challenge, Cyberabad Moves 2026 The problem: at KPHB Colony the other side is 13 m across, but the legal way round is 1.58 km to drive. What we found: all 10 directions we drove matched our model, none failed; 7 under rules written down before driving. What it costs: about ₹12,699 a year for a two-wheeler commuter on a 1.75 km detour, counting fuel, wear and time (the calculator's starting example; change any number). The Hi-Tech City loop: today's distances for all 20

A one-way loop can make traffic flow faster and still make many trips longer: a trip that today runs against the loop's direction has to go round it. Speed and density measure the first. Nothing in the published plans measures the second. When the KBR Park one-way loop was made permanent in 2026, we could find no published before-and-after figures for distance or travel time. The distance is the part a resident feels every day, in fuel, time and the extra kilometres buses and office shuttles run. It is also the part that open data can measure well.

Driving distance between every pair of loop points, on today's roads and on the loop as proposed, from OpenStreetMap with a published method. Bus route length for every TGSRTC route that uses a loop road against its direction, from the open GTFS feed on Open Data Telangana. Before, during and after: a baseline now, the same trips driven during the trial at the same hours, and again once it is permanent. Published whatever they show. We make no claim about walking. OpenStreetMap's footpath and crossing data for Hyderabad is not complete enough to support one, so we leave it out rather than guess.

pages.title: where it goes next: plans, open to pilot partners

s.t: One phase is live today in Hyderabad. The next two are planned and open to city teams who want to try them with us. Nothing here is a promise of dates.

s.h: Phase 1 · Live today: the Hyderabad pilot
s.t: Every crossing in our sample modelled from open map data, ten driven directions checked on the road, an open cost calculator, a baseline for all 20 trips between the five proposed Hi-Tech City loop points, and a way to report a changed median opening. See the entry · See the drives · Try the calculator

s.h: Phase 2 · Planned: the rest of Hyderabad
s.t: For What it would do Status Citizens A phone-friendly web tool, nothing to install: tap any proposed U-turn or closure and see the extra distance and cost for your own trip. Report a gap, a queue or a dark stretch with a blurred photo. Planned Traffic and city teams A separate, signed-in sandbox in the browser: try a closure or a one-way change on a copy of the map before barriers go down, see car, shuttle and bus detours, and export standard GeoJSON and GTFS files for existing control-room tools. Planned · in exploration Why web first and not an app: commuters already carry navigation apps and teams already run several systems. A web tool needs no install and no app-store review, and works on any phone.

s.h: Phase 3 · Planned: Bengaluru, then other Indian cities
s.t: The same open method, open map and open bus data, starting with Bengaluru's corridors, then offered as a free toolkit to any city mapped on OpenStreetMap.

s.h: What the city could do, now and later
s.t: Our recommendations, drawn from the drives. Each one can be measured before and after; arcroad will drive the same stretches again and publish the change. Now: 0 to 6 months, low cost Later: 1 to 5 years Sign every legal U-turn 300 m ahead, so drivers stop cutting lanes at the last second Underpasses and foot over bridges where people now cross NH-65 on foot Peak-hour marshals at the worst U-turn queues Junction redesign on the busiest corridors, with a safe crossing for every signal removed A written reason and a review date for every closed median opening A maximum distance between legal turning points in built-up areas Continuous median railings where crossing on foot is unsafe Parking checked on site before a licence is granted Signed, lit and marshalled diversions at every road works Live closures and U-turn changes shared with navigation apps Vending zones set back from the carriag

s.h: Who adds friction to a crossing
s.t: A long detour is rarely one party's fault. This is a map of who and what adds to it, and what we can measure today. We have no counts yet to say which matters most, so we show no percentages. Source of friction How it shows up Measured by arcroad today Where U-turns are placed Metres across becomes kilometres to drive Yes: modelled and driven U-turn queues Turning traffic blocks a through lane Partly: crawl minutes at hotspots, queue photos Road works and diversions Unsigned or unlit detours Partly: crawl minutes and photos Vendors and parking on the carriageway A lane lost, walkers pushed into traffic Photos only Breakdowns A sudden lane loss with no warning Not yet Wrong-side driving The shortcut that puts others at risk Not yet; what studies show People crossing on foot with no safe crossing Risky crossings across fast traffic Not yet; planned counts Night glare Seconds driven blind T

s.h: A lesson from the Outer Ring Road
s.t: The Outer Ring Road avoids the crossing problem by design: it has no at-grade turns, only interchanges, with service roads alongside for local trips. That is why we leave it out of our sample. A city loop cannot be built like an expressway, but two of its ideas carry over where a loop is unavoidable: a service lane for short local hops, and a grade-separated U-turn at the busiest point, so turning traffic does not queue in a through lane. Whether either fits a given junction is for the city's engineers; the loop baseline on the entry page is where that discussion can start.

s.h: Every road as clear as the Outer Ring Road
s.t: On the Outer Ring Road a driver always knows what comes next: numbered exits, signs well before each one, and the same rules for every lane. Our main junctions and loops rarely give that warning. A driver often learns that a road has turned one-way, or where the next U-turn is, only on reaching it. The aim for the years ahead is that every road, a single carriageway, a divided road or a loop, reads just as clearly. Name and number every junction and U-turn opening on a corridor, the way expressway exits are numbered. Signs, maps, complaints and news reports all point to the same place. Advance signs before every loop or one-way stretch, showing the loop and the distance to the next U-turn. Time to pick a lane, instead of a late swerve. One public map for each loop: direction, entry and exit points, U-turn openings, open for map apps to use. Phone directions that match the road on the day

The stages, and the info button Stage On the road 0 Announced Nothing yet; a tender or works order exists 1 Mobilised Barricades, board, machinery, no digging 2 Dug Trench, road cut, utilities being moved 3 Structure rising Piers, girders, culvert boxes 4 Finishing Surface laid, markings missing 5 Open Barricades gone, speeds back to normal 6 Stalled No change on two visits 30+ days apart 7 Left half-done Stalled 6+ months, or closed on paper unfinished

s.h: Parking pushed onto the road designed
s.t: A commercial building is approved on condition that it provides its own parking. When that parking is missing, converted to shops or storage, or charged for, the cars go onto the public road, and everyone else pays: fewer lanes, slower traffic, walkers pushed into the carriageway. An oncoming high beam blinds the person facing it, and the eye takes time to recover. Take the driver's seat → · The evidence. Anything permanent in the road, recorded by what it does ("narrows 3 lanes to 2"), never by what it is or who owns it. DetailsCovers structures, transformers, poles, kiosks and trees. Study · pre-registered 11 Nov 2026 · running

Some median openings on our divided roads sit just before or just after a junction, or a short distance from another opening. Each one adds a place where vehicles cut across the fast lane or wait in it. We are finding them from open data across the Cyberabad IT corridor, checking a sample on the road, and publishing only what that check confirms. 1area first: the Cyberabad IT corridor, Gachibowli to Madhapur10flagged openings checked on the road before any figure is published0results published yet: the study is running

A median opening is a gap in the divider of a divided road where vehicles can turn across. Guidance on access control (IRC:62) wants openings at intersections, and spaced well apart elsewhere. So each opening falls into one of three groups. Not flaggedAt a junctionWithin 30 m of a crossing road or a signal. The opening is the junction itself, which is where guidance wants it. Second lookNext to a junction30 to 100 m from one. Close enough to add a second crossing point to the junction's own queue. Second lookClose to another openingLess than 150 m from the next mid-block opening on the same road, so two gaps do the work of one.

We will not say that an opening causes a jam or an accident, or that it is unnecessary. Open data has no traffic speeds, vehicle counts or crash records for these points, so it cannot carry that weight. We say which openings are worth a second look, and why, so that the people responsible can look. We make no claim about walking: OpenStreetMap's footpath and crossing data for Hyderabad is not complete enough.

Ten flagged openings are drawn at random, with the random seed written down before the draw, and checked on the road or in dated photos. If at least seven of the ten are real openings that match the map, the full result is published here with the check. If fewer than seven are, the result is withdrawn and we publish that instead: it would mean the map, not the road, is the problem. 11 Nov 2026 · Method fixed in writingDefinitions, thresholds, the hypothesis, the competing explanation and the ground check, written before any data was read. 11 Nov 2026 · One rule corrected, openlyA test of the code on a small area showed the first rule flagged openings that are the junction itself. The fix (the 30 m line above) is dated in the method, made before the study run, and those test numbers are not published. pages.title: blinded by the light: what an oncoming high beam does to your eyes

s.t: Take the driver's seat on a divided road at night. Someone is about to step out of the median gap ahead. An oncoming car keeps its high beam on. Tap "I see someone" the moment you see them. What you can see of the personPerson visible100% Glare in your eyeGlare0 cd/m² Oncoming car · Car —Person ahead · Person — 60km/h Oncoming car's lights Your age Your speed Road

s.h: What just happened to your eyes
s.t: Scattered lightLight from a bright lamp scatters inside the eye and lays a veil over everything near it. A dark figure against a dark road loses its contrast first. Worse with ageThe scattered veil grows with the fourth power of age: at 65 it is about twice as strong as at 25 for the same lamp. Slow to recoverAfter the lamp passes, the eye stays dazzled for seconds. At 60 km/h every second is almost 17 metres. Rain makes it worseA wet road mirrors each headlamp into a long streak, and the road markings vanish under it.

Rule 106 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules requires headlamps that can be dipped so they do not dazzle the driver of an oncoming vehicle. Fines are under section 177 of the Motor Vehicles Act. A median screen or hedge on divided roads blocks the beam altogether. How this is built, and its limits The glare is computed, not painted. For every pixel, every frame, the veil of light scattered in the eye is worked out with the CIE General Disability Glare Equation (CIE 146:2002): Lveil/E = 10/θ³ + (5/θ² + 0.1p/θ)(1 + (A/62.5)⁴) + 0.0025p, with θ the angle in degrees between your line of sight and each lamp, A your age and p = 0.5 for brown eyes. The light reaching your eye from each lamp is its intensity divided by the distance squared, using typical values: 30,000 cd a lamp on high beam and 500 cd a lamp on dipped beam towards an oncoming driver. "What you can see of the person" is their lu
